title: Korean Female Named Sai Gyoku-Jo, A Dancing Partner

page_data.en:
FM. 2

N.K.
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
S. 2. Special Branch. Station,
REPORT
Date November 10, 1936.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. B. REGISTRY
File No. 2601

Subject Korean Female named Sai Gyoku-Jo, A Dancing Partner.

Made by D. S. Kamashita Forwarded by J. [Signature]

With reference to the attached translation of an article from the "Shanghai Mainichi" on the subject of a Korean dancing partner arrested for revolutionary activities, I have to state that the information is incorrect and that the following information has been obtained from the local Japanese Consular Police:-

A Korean dancing partner named Sai Gyoku-Jo (崔玉女), aged 24, native of Heijo, has been in the employ of the Metropole Dancing Hall for some time.

The local Japanese Consular Police recently received information from the Heijo Police, Korea, to the effect that this female went to Heijo on holiday in the summer of this year and during her stay in Heijo she received a remittance, a sum of Yen 500, from a certain foreigner employed by a sewing machine Co. in Tokyo, and that she wrote a letter to the foreigner to the effect that she was going to Shanghai shortly afterwards. The Consular Police were requested to make necessary investigations regarding the female, because the Heijo Police suspected she might have been engaged in espionage work.

On receipt of the information, the Consular Police summoned her to the Consulate on November 4. Since that time she has been detained at the Consulate. During the course of interrogation she admitted having received the remittance from the foreigner in Tokyo and also having written a letter to him during her stay in Heijo. She, however, stated that she had fallen in love with the foreigner when he resided in Shanghai and they had continued to correspond with each other. She also told the officer that as her family was very poor she had obtained monetary assistance amounting to the sum of Yen 2,000

（印：SPECIAL BRANCH SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE 11 NOV. 1936）

日期：1936年11月10日。

上海公共租界工部局警务处
特别支部登记处
档案编号：2601

事由：名为崔玉女（Sai Gyoku-Jo）的朝鲜籍舞女。

撰写人：D. S. Kamashita 转呈人：J. [签名]

关于附上的《上海每日新闻》（Shanghai Mainichi）一篇报道的译文，该报道涉及一名因从事革命活动而被捕的朝鲜籍舞女，本人须声明该信息有误，且已从日本驻沪领事馆警察处获得如下信息：

一名名为崔玉女（Sai Gyoku-Jo）的朝鲜籍舞女，现年24岁，咸兴（Heijo）人，已在麦特罗波利坦舞厅（Metropole Dancing Hall）受雇一段时间。

日本驻沪领事馆警察近期收到来自朝鲜咸兴警方的情报，称该女子于今年夏季前往咸兴度假，在咸兴停留期间，她收到一笔来自东京某缝纫机公司任职的外国人的汇款，金额为500日元，并且她曾致信该外国人，表示不久后将前往上海。由于咸兴警方怀疑其可能从事间谍工作，故请求领事馆警察对该女子进行必要调查。

收到该情报后，领事馆警察于11月4日传唤其至领事馆。自那时起，她一直被拘留在领事馆。在审讯过程中，她承认收到了来自东京该外国人的汇款，并承认在咸兴停留期间曾致信给他。然而，她声称在该外国人居住上海时与其相爱，此后双方一直保持通信。她还向警官表示，由于其家境贫寒，她获得了总计2,000日元的金钱援助

（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处特别支部 1936年11月11日）

November 9, 1936. Morning Translation.

MAINICHI

KOREAN DANCING PARTNER ARRESTED FOR REVOLUTIONARY
ACTIVITIES

On November 4 a Korean dancing
partner named Choi Bok Shun, age 22, of the St. George's
Dance Hall, was arrested by the Japanese Consular Police
for collecting funds for the Korean independence movement.
She is now undergoing a close examination at the hands of
the Japanese Consular Police.

NIPPO, MAINICHI AND NICHI-NICHI

ANTI-JAPANESE FRONT FORMED BY THE 29TH ARMY AND
STUDENTS.

Peiping, November 8.
Recently 72 school and university
professors issued an anti-Japanese manifesto; the army and
the people held a mass meeting; students dispatched a
circular telegram; the anti-Japanese activities among the Chinese
people have become more noticeable. The students have
formed a united anti-Japanese front with the soldiers of
the 29th Army. Their activities will obstruct the efforts
of the Charhar-Hopei Political Council to bring about Sino-
Japanese rapprochement and the economic development of the
North.

The professors and students
of the Normal School will issue an anti-Japanese circular
telegram shortly.

About 1,000 students of the
Chinghwa and Yenking Universities held a meeting and
delivered anti-Japanese speeches after attending the military
manoeuvres of the 29th Army.

On November 7 and 8 about 100
students of the Normal School visited several villages near
Peiping and delivered anti-Japanese addresses and distributed
anti-Japanese handbills relating to the military manoeuvres
of the Japanese army in the North.

The students of the Chinghwa
University sent representatives to request General Fo Tso
Yih, Chairman of the Suiyuan Provincial Government, to
organize a united anti-Japanese front of the army and people
for defence of the province.

Several representatives of
universities have been dispatched to the South to submit
an anti-Japanese petition to the Central Government.

1936年11月9日。晨间译文。

《每日新闻》

朝鲜籍舞女因从事革命活动被捕

11月4日，圣乔治舞厅（St. George's Dance Hall）一名名为崔福顺（Choi Bok Shun）、现年22岁的朝鲜籍舞女，被日本领事馆警察逮捕，罪名是为朝鲜独立运动筹集资金。目前她正接受日本领事馆警察的严密审查。

《日本日报》、《每日新闻》及《日日新闻》

第29军与学生组成抗日阵线。

北平，11月8日。
近日，72名中小学及大学教授发表抗日宣言；军民举行群众大会；学生发出通电；中国民众的抗日活动日益显著。学生们已与第29军士兵结成统一的抗日阵线。他们的活动将阻碍察哈尔-河北政治委员会促成中日亲善及华北经济发展的努力。

师范学校的教授和学生即将发出抗日通电。

清华大学和燕京大学约1,000名学生在参加第29军的军事演习后举行集会，并发表抗日演讲。

11月7日和8日，师范学校约100名学生走访了北平附近的几个村庄，发表抗日演说，并分发有关日军在华北进行军事演习的抗日传单。

清华大学学生派出代表，请求绥远省政府主席傅作义将军组织军民统一的抗日阵线，以保卫该省。

多所大学已派出数名代表南下，向中央政府提交抗日请愿书。
